title: Sunrise cache hacks — reading & experiment plan
content:
Morning scribbles after skimming 3 papers while coffee-steaming. Want to capture the high-level ideas and a tiny, runnable experiment plan for the week.

Why I care (short):
- We keep losing quality on >8k contexts once we aggressively quantize and shard KVs.
- Potential mitigation: lightweight prefetch + short-lived local prefix caches to reduce misses for repeated turn patterns.
- Secondary win: reduce CPU overhead on host routing by serving more from hot caches.

Top takeaways from readings:
1) "Latent prefix caching for episodic retrieval" (arXiv 2601.01234) — uses a small projection table to store compressed prefixes and rehydrate to full KV with minimal decode cost. Key note: a 4-8 token prefix often recovers >60% of attention mass for chat-like loops. Practically: store compressed prefixes per conversation and use a cheap decoder-only reweighting to decide to fetch full KVs.
2) "Staggered prefetch and eviction" (conf talk notes) — prefetch based on session heuristics (recency + token-pattern signatures) and evict by estimated reuse. Suggested low-overhead signature: last-4-token hash + turn length bucket.
3) "Quant-aware KV tiling" — aligning KV shards with quant blocks to reduce dequant overhead on partial loads. The paper suggests marginal latency improvements when shaded requests hit the aligned shard.

Quick sketch: sunrise-cache idea
- Keep a tiny L1 per-worker: up to 256 compressed prefix entries, compressed with a learned projection (64-d) and stored in LRU with occasional frequency boosting for repeating signatures.
- On request: compute 4-token signature, check L1; if hit -> fast shortpath: supply small rehydration vector to runtime (no full KV load). If miss -> tag for background prefetch (if session qualifies) and serve from main path.
- Fallback: when quality drop detected, auto-increase prefix budget for that session.

Experiment plan (minimal repro)
- Data: sample 10k multi-turn sessions from internal convo-corpus (mix of short helpers and long instruction threads).
- Baselines: no prefix cache, naive LRU prefix cache (exact-token match), and sunrise learned-proj cache (this sketch).
- Metrics: generation perplexity delta on >=8k context vs baseline, median tail latency (95/99), and prefetch CPU% (on serving host). Also track cache hit rate by session type.
- Toy runtime harness: reuse local 'kv-shim' harness in repo linked above. Implement projection with a tiny MLP (64 -> 64) trained for reconstruction loss from full KVs (2 epochs on a 50k sample).

Checklist (short-term):
- [ ] wire up token-signature extractor in kv-shim (Eliot)
- [ ] prototype compressed prefix store API and LRU (Maya)
- [ ] quick trainer for projection (Nora)
- [ ] run 1k-session smoke tests for correctness and perf profiling
- [ ] gather quality snapshots (diff w/ baseline)

Open questions / risks:
- How much extra memory for rehydration vectors? If too large, we lose the cost win. Need tight budget: aim for <1.5MB per worker.
- Training projection stability: cold-start will be rough; maybe use PCA init and 1 epoch of distillation from full KV retrieval.
- Security/PII: caching conversation prefixes could persist sensitive data; ensure ephemeral keys and TTL policy.
- Routing interplay: dedicated vs shared pools — prefetch tax might be paid differently depending on pricing model. Need to simulate cost-per-token impact.

Debug signals to surface in Console:
- prefix_cache_hit_rate by model + session_type
- avg_rehydrate_time (ms)
- fallback_increase_count (per session)
- quality_regression_alerts (by prompt set)

Tiny timeline:
- Day 0-2: prototype store + signature extractor, smoke test locally
- Day 3-5: train projection and integrate rehydration shortpath; smoke perf runs
- Day 6-10: 10k-session bench, gather metrics, iterate eviction policy

Notes-to-self: keep the first prototype as dumb as possible. We don't need production durability; ephemeral L1 in process only. If hits look promising, push a small alloc to a single dedicated pool and run A/B on a shallow route.

Slack refs / next steps: ping @eliot for signature PR, @maya for store pattern, open a short RFC if baseline beats by >1.5% perplexity with 20% latency cut.

Random scribbles:
- Could we use hashed-turn embeddings as keys rather than token-4 signatures? Trade-off: more compute to embed turn, but more robust to paraphrase.
- Consider fallthrough TTL = min(30s, session_idle * 2) instead of fixed 60s.

End of morning sprint; saving this before a meeting. Will refine after prototyping.

-- Nora
